title: feat(authz-ux): surface ADR-0066 posture / per-op requiredPermissions / capability lint in authoring UI
body:
## What & why

The framework side of the authorization gap map (framework#2561) just landed three ADR-0066 authoring-surface primitives — ④ secure-by-default posture (framework#2691 flipped 6 system objects to `access.default:'private'`), ⑤ per-operation `requiredPermissions`, and ⑨ the capability-reference lint (framework#2690). This PR makes them **visible and editable where admins actually work**, closing the objectui half of ④ ("surface each object's posture visibly in Studio") plus the ⑤/⑨ authoring UX.

## Changes

### 1. Access matrix — Private-posture badge (④)

`PermissionMatrixEditor` object rows now show an amber **Private** badge when the object declares `access: { default: 'private' }`, with a tooltip explaining that a permission set's `'*'` wildcard grant does **not** cover the object (an explicit grant or View/Modify All Records is required). Without this, an admin reading the matrix assumes a wildcard-only set reaches the object while the server 403s. `ObjectSummary` threads `access.default` through the catalog mapping.

### 2. Object designer — Access section (④ + ⑤)

`ObjectDefaultInspector` (shared by metadata-admin and the Studio Data-pillar settings tab) gains an **Access** section:

- **Exposure posture** select (`public` / `private`); the private hint warns that some permission set must grant the object before publishing, or only platform admins can use it. Choosing `public` clears the key (spec default) instead of writing it out.
- **Required capabilities** editor for the object-level `requiredPermissions` AND-gate. Supports both shapes: `string[]` (all operations) and the per-operation `{read, create, update, delete}` map (⑤), with lossless mode conversion (all→per-op copies the list into every operation so nothing silently loosens; per-op→all unions).
- The per-operation toggle is **feature-detected** against the bundled `@objectstack/spec` (the ⑤ union ships in spec ≥ 12.7): on today's pinned spec the toggle stays hidden so the UI never authors a shape client-side Zod validation would reject; it lights up automatically on the dependency bump. Map-form drafts always render per-operation inputs regardless (mode is derived from the value shape).

### 3. Publish flow — capability-reference lint (⑨)

`usePublishAllDrafts` now runs `validateCapabilityReferences` (`@objectstack/lint`, new dependency) over the pending object/app/action drafts before publish, with the declaration side assembled from **published permission sets ∪ pending permission drafts**, and surfaces "capability registered nowhere" findings as a warning toast. Strictly advisory and fail-safe by design:

- the rule itself is feature-detected (the pinned `@objectstack/lint@12.6.0` predates it → silent no-op until the bump; zero code change needed),
- any client/import/rule failure is swallowed — the lint can never break or block publishing (a capability may legitimately be provided by another installed package; the reference fails closed at runtime anyway).

## i18n

All new strings shipped in both `en-US` and `zh-CN`.

## Tests / verification

- New/extended suites: matrix badge case (badge on the private row only, tooltip content), Access section (posture patch + clear-to-default, array-form editing, map-form per-op editing, feature-detect hides the toggle on the older bundled spec), `capabilityLint` (pseudo-stack assembly incl. published∪draft permissions, non-linted-type no-op, error swallowing, real feature-detect no-op path).
- **590 tests green** across the touched directories (74 files); `@object-ui/app-shell` `type-check` clean; full workspace `pnpm build` green.
- Progressive-enhancement note for reviewers: the ⑤ toggle and ⑨ warnings become active when `@objectstack/spec` / `@objectstack/lint` are bumped to the next framework release; both paths are already covered by tests via the injection seams.

Refs objectstack-ai/framework#2561 (ADR-0066 ④/⑤/⑨) · framework#2690 · framework#2691
